samples.summary: The table-cell branch of getVisualLineRange got the same affinity change but has no test at all
samples.evidence: getVisualLineRange's cell-block path (text-editor.ts:4019-4034) now computes `ownsLineEnd = li === endLine - 1 || lineAffinity === 'backward'`. The new integration test (test/view/visual-line-affinity.test.ts) builds a document of one plain paragraph block (`store.setDocument({ blocks: [makeBlock(TEXT)] })`), so `getCellInfo` returns undefined and this branch is never entered; the unit tests in visual-line.test.ts only exercise `findVisualLine`, which is the non-cell path. Nothing asserts Home/End/Cmd+Backspace at a wrap boundary inside a wrapped table cell.
searchedFor: grep 'Home|handleEnd|\'End\'' in packages/docs/test (only visual-line-affinity.test.ts and cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts)

samples.summary: New explicit `lineAffinity` parameters on getVisualLineStart/End/Range are never passed non-default by any caller or test
samples.evidence: All three call sites (text-editor.ts:2786, 2799, 2845) rely on the `this.cursor.lineAffinity` default; no test passes an explicit affinity either (these are private methods, and the new test drives them only through key events). So the added parameter path itself is unexercised — a wrong explicit-argument plumbing could not be detected by the suite.

samples.summary: No integration test for the 'forward' affinity direction (the behavior that must be preserved)
samples.evidence: All four editor-level tests reach the boundary via `End`, which leaves affinity 'backward' (cursor.moveTo default, cursor.ts:28). The complementary case — arriving at the same boundary offset with 'forward' affinity (e.g. ArrowRight onto the boundary, or handleHome's explicit `moveTo(newPos, 'forward')`), where Home/End must resolve to the *later* visual line — is asserted only at the pure-function level in visual-line.test.ts, never through the editor. A regression that made getVisualLineStart always resolve 'backward' would still pass this suite.

samples.summary: First test asserts only setup preconditions, not the changed behavior
samples.evidence: `it('End lands exactly on the wrap boundary...')` asserts `cursorOffset > 0` and `< TEXT.length` — true both before and after the fix (pre-fix End also stopped inside the block). It is a useful guard that the canvas shim/wrapping/onCursorMove plumbing works (without it, tests 2 and 3 could pass vacuously with cursorOffset stuck at 0), but it does not itself cover the affinity change despite its title.

samples.summary: Only character-level wrapping is covered; space-wrapped lines (the common case, which interacts with getVisualLineEnd's trailing-space trim) are untested
samples.evidence: TEXT is `'x'.repeat(400)` — a single token, forcing character-granularity wrapping so End lands exactly on the boundary. For normal space-wrapped text, getVisualLineEnd trims trailing spaces (text-editor.ts:4067-4073) so End lands before the boundary; no test covers Home/End/Cmd+Backspace on such a line under either affinity.
